# Shehbaz Sharif, Pakistan (2024): 2B.10 evidence note

Overall read: **mildly favorable, low-to-moderate confidence**. Inherited conditions were poor: a hung election, economic fragility, Kashmir tension, and a coercive domestic political environment. Against that backdrop, Sharif’s 2024 record is somewhat better on diplomacy, de-escalation, and institutional restraint than on raw conflict rhetoric. I did **not** find evidence that he left the region decisively more peaceful, but I did find repeated lawful / dialogue-oriented gestures that point modestly in that direction.

| Polarity | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Favorable | Peace in South Asia depends on settlement of Kashmir dispute: PM | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-21 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/21-09-2024/peace-in-south-asia-depends-on-settlement-of-kashmir-dispute-pm | Sharif said Pakistan believes in peace and stability through dialogue, and that lasting regional peace depends on a peaceful Kashmir settlement. This is direct evidence of a more lawful, diplomatic posture than inherited escalation. | 2B.10; also 2B.1, 2B.3, 2B.6, 1B.8 |
| Favorable | PM urges UN to take action against Israel’s genocidal acts | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-26 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/26-09-2024/pm-urges-un-to-take-action-against-israels-genocidal-acts | In UNGA remarks, Sharif urged confidence-building measures to prevent war between major powers and ease tensions. That is de-escalatory language consistent with a more stable regional/international posture. | 2B.10; also 2B.1, 2B.3, 2B.6, 1B.8 |
| Favorable / institutional | Arms Control And Disarmament | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | standing page; current version cites a May 2024 update | https://mofa.gov.pk/arms-control-and-disarmament | Pakistan’s official policy page says it supports CTBT objectives, a unilateral testing moratorium, FMCT negotiations, IAEA safeguards, reciprocal inspections proposals, UNSCR 1540 implementation, export controls, and multilateral nonproliferation norms. This is a strong signal of lawful restraint and institutionalization. | 2B.10; also 1B.4, 1B.6, 1B.7, 1B.9 |
| Favorable / institutional | 6th Round of Pakistan-UK Dialogue on Arms Control and Non-Proliferation | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | 2024-05-16 | https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/6th-round-of-pakistan-uk-dialogue-on-arms-control-non-proliferation | Pakistan held a formal arms-control and nonproliferation dialogue with the UK and pledged continued coordination on UN, CD, IAEA, and OPCW issues. This points to stable, rules-based external relations rather than conflict expansion. | 2B.10; also 1B.4, 1B.6, 1B.7 |
| Favorable / institutional | Pakistan-China Bilateral Consultations on Arms Control and Nonproliferation | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | 2024-09-14 | https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/pakistan-china-bilateral-consultations-on-arms-control-and-nonproliferation | Pakistan sustained structured consultations covering global/regional security, cyber, AI, outer space, peaceful nuclear technology, and treaty forums. This is evidence of continued lawful engagement with major partners on risk domains. | 2B.10; also 1B.4, 1B.7, 1B.9 |
| Favorable | The visit of UN Disarmament Fellows to Pakistan | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | 2024-10-21 | https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/the-visit-of-un-disarmament-fellows-to-pakistan | Pakistan briefed UN disarmament fellows on arms control, disarmament, nonproliferation, and nuclear safety/security architecture. That is a transparency signal, not a conflict-justifying one. | 2B.10; also 1B.4, 1B.7, 1B.9 |
| Favorable | Pakistan's nuclear programme is for peaceful purposes: PM | Radio Pakistan | 2024-12-24 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/24-12-2024/pm-vows-to-root-out-scourge-of-terrorism | Sharif publicly framed Pakistan’s nuclear posture as defensive, self-defensive, and non-aggressive. That is consistent with a more lawful and stable regional posture than an openly coercive one. | 2B.10; also 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.5, 2B.6 |
| Mixed / negative | PM stresses for peaceful solution of global challenges | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-27 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/27-09-2024/pm-urges-india-to-engage-in-dialogue-for-resolution-of-jk-dispute | The same UNGA speech that urged dialogue also warned Pakistan would “respond most decisively” to Indian aggression and described India’s war doctrine in nuclearized terms. This kept relations tense and limits any claim that 2024 was purely peace-improving. | 2B.10; also 1B.1, 1B.2, 2B.3, 2B.6 |
| Mixed / context | Pakistan election-day internet shutdown is a reckless attack on people’s rights | Amnesty International | 2024-02-08 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/pakistan-election-day-internet-shutdown-is-a-reckless-attack-on-peoples-rights/ | Amnesty condemned the election-day telecom and mobile internet shutdown as a rights violation. This is domestic rather than external-relations evidence, but it indicates a coercive environment at accession, which tempers the “more lawful” assessment. | 2B.10; also 1B.8, 2B.6 |

## Synthesis

- Best-supported conclusion: Sharif left Pakistan’s external posture **somewhat more stable and lawful at the institutional level** than what he inherited, mainly through dialogue-first Kashmir rhetoric and sustained arms-control / nonproliferation engagement.
- The improvement is **modest**, not decisive. He did not resolve Kashmir, normalize ties with India, or fully purge brinkmanship from his rhetoric.
- On balance, 2024 looks **slightly better than inherited** in terms of lawful / diplomatic posture, but still constrained by inherited conflict, regional rivalry, and his own hard-edged public messaging.
